problem: Navigation policies are embodiment-specific: a policy trained on one robot fails on another, even with small changes in body size or camera viewpoint. Cross-embodiment real-world datasets cover only ~20 embodiments, too few for robust generalization.
motivation: Custom robot hardware is increasingly common, so retraining a navigation policy per robot is costly. Simulation can generate effectively unlimited embodiment diversity, so massive embodiment randomization may yield a single policy that transfers zero-shot to unseen real robots.
key_idea: Train an end-to-end object-goal navigation transformer (IL then RL) in AI2-THOR on ~1M randomly sampled embodiments (collider size, rotation pivot, 1-2 cameras with random pose/FoV/aspect) so it transfers zero-shot to unseen real robots.
insight: Embodiment diversity at scale is what matters: policies trained on narrower ranges of individual parameters (50k embodiments) lose ~13% average SR versus the full-range policy (59.1 vs 72.1 SR). The policy infers its body implicitly from visual cues and collisions (e.g. tries to go under a bed with a low camera but tall body, collides, reroutes), a behavior that emerges in RL and not in the expert data. Explicitly conditioning on embodiment parameters gave no clear benefit (SR 67.62 vs 69.44, collision rate not improved), and a stronger visual encoder (CLIP ViT-L/14) gave about +9% SR.
method: Embodiment randomization: the agent body is an invisible collider box (size 0.2-0.5 x 0.3-1.5 x 0.2-0.5 m), with a random rotation pivot and 1-2 RGB cameras with random position, pitch, yaw, FoV and resolution. 1M such embodiments are sampled.

Expert data generation: safety-aware A* planner over per-embodiment reachable grids. Cost is the inverse cube of clipped distance to the nearest obstacle, waypoints are extracted and interpolated to the action space. Trajectories come from 50k ProcTHOR houses with Objaverse objects.

Architecture (PoliFormer-style): frozen SigLIP-ViT-B/16 image encoder and text encoder, images padded to square and resized to 256x256, second camera zero-masked when absent. A 3-layer Transformer State Encoder with a STATE token feeds a 3-layer causal Transformer Decoder with KV-cache, then a linear actor-critic head.

Training (FLaRe recipe): IL on 1M-embodiment expert trajectories (batch 240, context 100, 80k iterations, 8xH100), then DD-PPO RL for 40M steps on randomized embodiments with entropy loss disabled. Reward is distance shaping plus success reward 10 minus a 0.01 step penalty.
Platform-agnostic discrete action space: MoveBase ±20cm, RotateBase ±6°/±30°, Done, executed by robot-specific low-level controllers on real robots.

Optional adaptations: RL fine-tuning up to 20M steps for embodiment-specialized policies, a 0.1 collision penalty to halve the collision rate, and an embodiment-conditioned variant (19-dim parameter vector as an extra token).

setting.backbone: SigLIP-ViT-B/16 (frozen) + Transformer state encoder + causal Transformer decoder actor-critic (trained IL then RL)
setting.training_data: 1M randomized-embodiment expert A* trajectories in 50k ProcTHOR houses (Objaverse objects), then 40M steps of RL on randomized embodiments; no real robot data
setting.observation: 1-2 egocentric RGB images (random camera parameters) + object-category language goal; no depth, no odometry
setting.simulator: AI2-THOR (ProcTHOR houses, Objaverse) with a custom randomized-embodiment extension
setting.privileged: none (embodiment parameters not given to the policy at test time)

numbers_note: No standard VLN/ObjectNav benchmark from the canonical list is used; benchmarks are CHORES-S (ProcTHOR/AI2-THOR) and custom real-world sets. The embodiment-specialized fine-tuning results appear only in a figure.
results: A single policy trained on 1M random embodiments reaches 72.1% average SR across 5 simulated embodiments (+16.7% absolute over the best single-embodiment baseline average, PoliFormer-LoCoBot 55.4 per the table's comparison) and 78.9% on 4 real-world platforms. It matches or beats embodiment-specific policies, e.g. Unitree A1 72.0 vs 55.3 for PoliFormer trained on it. A collision penalty halves the collision rate, and a phone-guided human evaluation gets 73.3% vs FLaRe's 40.0%.
limitations: Only tested on object-goal navigation with a simple discrete action space; embodiments are limited to collider-box bodies and up to two RGB cameras.
Collisions occur more often on out-of-distribution embodiments, since the policy infers its body partly through contact; SR on unseen individual parameters is lower.
Explicit embodiment conditioning showed no clear benefit, so how best to use known embodiment information remains unresolved.
